items.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: I think of this band out in Santa Monica that was started by Ernest Clark I think, a trumpet virtuoso back in 1902 I think it was.

ctx.x: It’s unfortunate that the opportunities as far as the big band playing you know, are not nearly as plentiful as they used to be. I think there’s probably a lot more talented people out there that come out of schools and they’re scrambling for ways to show what they know and to go to the next level.

Well, I think of this band out in Santa Monica that was started by Ernest Clark I think, a trumpet virtuoso back in 1902 I think it was. He started this municipal band out there, © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

about 35 pieces. And within that band they had a regular big jazz band and then a small combo and chamber groups. And they were all on salary out there, and they had their own recording studio. Anyway, it was started from 1902 and as far as I know it’s still going today. And they bring in guest artists to either play or sing or whatever they do, and they back them up. And it seems like a lot of cities could do something like that rather than only thinking of a symphony orchestra, they could probably have…
